recipes.name: Easy As Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon crumbled dried thyme, or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Use a pizza cutter to slice the puff pastry into 8 equal-sized strips. Weave the strips into a square lattice and place on a greased baking sheet.
Bake in preheated oven until it just starts to brown, 10 to 15 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.
Place the frozen peas, carrots, and corn in a microwave-safe bowl and cook in the microwave until cooked but still firm, 5 to 10 minutes.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the milk and stir while cooking until the mixture is smooth. Add the thyme and continue to cook and stir until the mixture thickens. Stir in the cooked vegetables and the chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Cook until heated through, stirring frequently, 5 to 7 minutes.
Pour the chicken mixture into a 2-quart baking dish. Lay the pastry lattice on top. Bake in the preheated oven until the crust is golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy As Chicken Pot Pie
raw_recipe.description: A frozen puff pastry helps turn some frozen vegetables and chicken into a delicious pot pie.

review.reviewBody: I make a miniature version by placing using biscuits and ramekins so everyone can have the perfect amount of crust (top and bottom!). I peel flaky style Grand's biscuits in half, place 1 half in bottom of each ramekin, bake for 6 minutes, fill with pot pie mixture and top with the other half of the biscuit and bake for 10-12 minutes. This is the perfect pot pie recipe!

It’s a keeper. I used cream of chicken soup instead of making my own base, so that cut me a step. I also used mixed frozen veggies (any vegetables would do, not just carrots, peas, and corn). On top I rolled out a sheet of refrigerated canned croissant dough instead of frozen puff pastry, because it already had perforation holes, looked pretty, and didn’t require time to thaw, cut and weave, so that cut me yet another step. So, it was easy and the kids ate it. I didn’t care for the amount of thyme though... will either cut down on it or will use rosemary or poultry seasoning next time. Will also think about adding some more “oomph” to it, as overall it was a bit bland. However, this is a great base recipe and really easy to make. Thank you!

Great recipe. We made it but with quite a few changes: 1. we used Grands! flaky Biscuits instead of phyllo - cut each biscuit in half horizontally. Place on top of filling.
2. Used 1 cup milk and 1-1/4 cups broth instead of all milk.
3. Decreased thyme to 1/2 t. and added 1/2 t. each season salt and garlic salt.
4. Added sauteed onion (1/2 C) and sauteed sliced mushrooms (approx 6) to filling.
5. Used cooked carrots, peas and broccoli or cauliflower to measure 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 C. Eliminated corn and used 1/2 can potatoes (diced) instead.

We loved it! I added some Minced Garlic and Italian Seasoning to my Sauteed Chicken. And used Veg.all for the vegetables. All I had was Filo dough and we brushed butter between the layers. it turned out so Good.
Excellent. I added potatoes, my homemade broth in place of half the milk. A real treat with leftovers!

I doubled this recipe, making the recommended substitution of half the specified milk for low sodium chicken stock. I also made two pies, one with celery substituted for the peas. The peas offered a much better flavor, of course. I also highly recommend just making the filling and serving this with bread sticks, as I accidentally did. The results were subversive, tasty, and well worth making again.

Thanks for the recipe! I didnt follow exactly because I didnt have everything called for and also just to suit our tastes. I'm rating it a 5 because I'm sure it would taste just as good if followed to the T, and it is also a good idea and a good base recipe if you're picky :) I used frozen peas, fresh carrots and garlic and potatoes and microwaved covered with a little water about 5 minutes to steam all the veggies. Didn't have thyme, used 21 seasoning blend and eyeballed it. had about 1/2 cup leftover turkey gravy which my mom made for thanksgiving, used that, about 1/2 cup vegetable broth and 1 cup milk for the sauce and added flour till thickened. I also used the butter, juices and bits scraped from the pan I used to cook the chicken instead of using the 2tb butter. It was so so good! My husband who isnt crazy about chicken, loved it so much, he ate half of the pie! One more thing, I didnt bother with the cutting and weaving the crust. I just baked it till barely browning on sides and then laid it over the top of the dish with the corners hanging over the sides. Looked great that way too. Sorry for not rating the original recipe but i will try it that way too, it will be great!

I was looking for a pot pie recipe that didn't include cream soups or broth, since I had neither. This recipe fit the bill and was absolutely fantastic! It was shockingly delicious. I had to change a few things. Since I didn't have puff pastry I made pie crusts instead. Baked the bottom crust in the pie pan at 350 for 15 mn, then added the filling and covered it with the top crust. I also only had canned veggies. I used green beans, corn and sliced potates (from the can) cut up. I just added the veggies directly from the can to the creamed mixture. My family couldn't get enough!
Made some changes like cream of chicken soup 1 can & small amount of chicken broth. Made it for my daughter & her family. They said it was the best they ever had. Would definitely made it again

This was extremely tasty. I used some extras to make sure that there were enough flavors. I cooked diced potatoes and carrots (I didn't have any frozen) and then used a cup of the cooking water and added a chicken bullion cube. I substituted that cup of water for a cup of the milk. I also sauteed an onion with some chopped garlic and added that to the mix. For the crust I used low fat crescent rolls. Of course, now I don't know how the original recipe would be without my modifications but this will absolutely become a staple for me!! Thanks for the idea!

We did enjoy this pot pie because of the use of the puff pastry as the crust instead of the traditional pie crust. I did use fresh vegetables instead of frozen (carrots, potatoes and broccoli) and I boiled the chicken because I wanted it to be shredded instead of in chunks. Also, next time I will add more spices (garlic powder or crushed garlic, sage,etc..) because it was a little bland. I think it is a great starter recipe!!
My husband didn't care for the thyme in it... I replied, " Good! More for ME!!!"
Delicious. Added a little more corn to mine for the kids, but my four fussy boys gobbled it down. Great recipe. Thanks to whomever posted it.
Incredibly bland and I'm not picky. I even had pepper on it. I won't make it again and I'm going to have to add garlic powder and tarragon for the leftovers.

I made this recipe because I had a sheet of leftover puff pastry, but did not want to make a dessert. This was about the only recipe I could find that called for one sheet of puff pastry and was not a dessert. The recipe was fine, but didn't 
"wow" us. I would probably not make it again because puff pastry is expensive, and there are other, better chicken pot pie recipes.

Delicious pot pie. The only drawback I have is that we saved the remaining food for leftovers, which wasn't as good as the night before due to the puff pastry loosing it's fresh crispiness. 

So, when I make it again, I'll make just enough for the two of us or make the full recipe for whenever our daughter and her fiance or our son stops by.

The meal was absolutely delicious, I will definitely make it again.
Delicious! I did add a few seasonings but otherwise stayed to the recipe.
I used this recipe as something to follow. I absolutely loved the idea of pie crusts being cut into strips something I'll keep in mind in the future. I used leftover turkey instead

Me and my Husband made this today, it was really awesome he couldn't get enough. The only thing different I did was use half and half instead of milk and used the layers biscuits we couldn't find the pastry dough. I am glad we did though it was amazing.
An easy and delicious chicken pot pie recipe, that the whole family will love. I have been using this recipe for the last 5 years and still LOVE it!
